This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

Steps in this phase (18 left, ~2.7 h):

[ ] s4 (~10 min) Server routes in apps/console-web/plugins/skins/server/routes.py: GET skins (gallery list with coverage), GET state?scope=, POST use / back / restore / undo / scope. They go through the theme-manager routes and the skin-switch engine, with no second store
[ ] s5 (~8 min) Server tests for the routes: list, state per scope, use → back → restore → undo round trip, refusal of unknown scope or skin
[ ] s6 (~8 min) CLI apps/console-web/plugins/skins/skins-plugin.mjs (list | state | use | back | restore | undo | scope | open), calling the same REST routes, and register it so `axf skins-ui …` works
[ ] s7 (~9 min) MCP plugin commands (skins_list, skins_state, skins_use, skins_back, skins_restore, skins_undo, skins_scope) through plugin-commands, plus console actions skin.use / skin.back / skin.restore / skin.undo for AmberX voice
[ ] s8 (~10 min) Gallery screen apps/console-web/plugins/skins/web/SkinsScreen.tsx: a grid of every skin card (name, icon pack, coverage), built from framework controls and tokens only, with a TabGroup for scope (Hub / App / Screen / Plugin) and a SkinScope root
[ ] s9 (~10 min) Live preview pane: the selected skin is drawn in a scoped desktop frame and a phone-width frame side by side (SkinScope with the preview skin, no write until Use), with a desktop/phone toggle on a role=toolbar
[ ] s10 (~9 min) Action toolbar on the screen: one-tap Use skin, Back to skin, Restore to Default (confirm) and Undo (snackbar plus a button), wired to the REST routes. Toolbar has role=toolbar, aria-label and tap-to-confirm
[ ] s11 (~10 min) Per-scope picker: pick the app, the screen (ui:<view>) or the plugin from registries, show the inherited skin and where it comes from, with an Inherit / Follow hub switch per scope
[ ] s12 (~7 min) Deep links: console_show / console_open targets skins, skins/skin/<id>, skins/scope/<scope> and skins/preview/<id>?view=phone. Register them in the plugin's nav and help entries
[ ] s13 (~10 min) Quick skin switcher on the banner: a status-widget chip (current skin for this scope) whose popover lists skins with one-tap Use, Back and Undo. Add it to KNOWN_BANNERS with banner settings (label, icon, settingsTab)
[ ] s14 (~8 min) Context-menu entries (rt.addContextItems): Change skin here… on any view root and plugin root, opening the scope picker on that scope. Banner chip right-click gives Settings… / Change… / Move
[ ] s15 (~9 min) Settings sub-tab (Settings → Plugins → Skins) with the level toolbar: show the banner chip, default scope, undo window, preview viewport. Each setting is readable and settable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice
[ ] s16 (~8 min) Hook AppearancePanel in framework/libs/settings to the skin-switch engine, so its Use / Back / Restore match the plugin's, and add an Open Skins gallery link when the plugin is installed (capability check, no folder name)
[ ] s17 (~10 min) UI Review choices: build at least 3 options for the gallery layout and for the banner chip as assets under apps/console-web/plugins/skins/assets/<type>/, with a choices JSON
